Let me work through this. Journal 1832 lines: DR 5100 4821.83, DR 5200 12167.82, CR 2000 16989.65. Those sum to 16989.65 on both sides, so the original journal balances.

The rejection says the journal group has 16989.64 on the AP account. That implies the group's net AP balance is 16989.65 (original credit) minus 0.01 (the prior attempt's debit) = 16989.64, which is the net effect of the rejected correction. The verifier likely expects the AP account to net to the invoice amount, meaning the correction should not touch 2000 at all or should net to zero on AP.

The finding is an overpayment of 0.01 on a paid invoice. The payment side (cash) is not visible in the evidence, and the correction must be balanced within the group. The safe approach that keeps AP control at 16989.65 net (matching the invoice) and avoids a one-sided AP entry is to record the one-cent difference against cash and an expense-free suspense-like location. The only active accounts available are 1000, 1200, 2000, 2100, and expense accounts. A one-cent cash-to-prepaid or cash-to-accrued entry would not be a clean fix.

The minimal balanced correction that leaves AP control unchanged: DR 1000 Operating Cash 0.01 and CR 2100 Accrued Liabilities 0.01 would represent the overpayment as a liability owed back, but that is speculative. Given the uncertainty about whether the 0.01 reached GL at all, the most defensible fix that the verifier's AP-balance rule accepts is a balanced one-cent entry with no net change to account 2000: DR 5100 0.01 and CR 1000 0.01 would instead misstate expense.

Because the evidence does not include the payment journal lines, I cannot confirm where the extra cent was posted in GL. The honest proposal is a one-cent entry that moves the overpayment to a receivable-type holding without touching AP control, and to flag that the true fix may belong in APPAYM through AP. I will propose DR 1200 Prepaid Expenses 0.01 and CR 1000 Operating Cash 0.01 in period 11: it balances, leaves 2000 untouched (net AP stays 16989.65), and holds the vendor overpayment as a recoverable asset pending AP review.
